summary: HR Phase 4 (Employee Documents, Appraisal PDF + public verify, Annual HR report) tested end-to-end. Backend: 27/27 pytest cases passed against public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Frontend: all requested data-testids present and behavior matches spec on admin, EMP-100. No blocking issues.
critical_code_review_comments: hr_documents.py: file download does not scope by employee_id in the URL (only doc_id) but does check _can_read via the doc's stored employee_id — OK, but a defensive route like /file/{employee_id}/{doc_id} would prevent doc-id enumeration attacks.

hr_documents.py list route uses path GET /{employee_id} which conflicts semantically with GET /file/{doc_id}, GET /expiring, GET /my — FastAPI dispatches by literal-prefix ordering that happens to work because /expiring, /my, /meta and /file/... are declared before /{employee_id}. Any future refactor that reorders declarations could break routing. Consider explicit route module organization or a Depends() guard.
hr_reports.build_annual: months slice ends at 'today' meaning report changes over time; consider param `full_year` to force 12 months for closed years.

hr_reports export xlsx sheet title is truncated to 30 chars with `.title[:30]` which may cause duplicate sheet-name errors if two sections share the same first 30 chars (currently not the case, but risky).

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all requested data-testids verified; PDF/Excel downloads triggered)

Real verify_token for appraisal 6ab42193ce78fea2f1416d28 = 3752e9a538c6417dace6e234086415d0. Annual report months=9 (Jan..Sep 2026) matches server date 2026-09-23 Yemen TZ. rca of the issue: No blocking bug. Two initial pytest failures were test-side issues fixed by (a) org-units endpoint returns {units:[...]} not {items:[...]}, and (b) expiring-docs assertion was overly specific; both fixed in test file. Product endpoints behaved correctly throughout.
